newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir film shows holed module, damaged solar panel.
newsitem.headline: Mir film shows holed module, damaged solar panel.

text.p: The first clear film of the damaged Mir space station on Thursday showed a smooth round hole several centimetres wide in its punctured Spektr module and a solar panel which was missing about a fifth of its area.

Reporters watching the exterior shots, transmitted by the Russian-American crew during their latest communications window with Mission Control near Moscow, heard the cosmonauts laugh as they discussed how to repair the damage caused in a collision with an unmanned cargo craft on Wednesday.

Much of the conversation was inaudible to reporters due to poor atmospheric conditions. Communications between Mission Control and Mir are only possible for 20 to 30 minutes every couple of hours, depending on the station's orbit.

American astronaut Michael Foale could be heard saying, "OK, OK," in reply to a stream of inaudible questions from a NASA representative at the Korolyov Mission Control Centre. There were no pictures of the crew or the inside of the station.

A 72-strong commission, including Mir's chief designer and NASA officials, was meeting there at 0930 GMT to decide on the repair strategy after the incident, which Russian space experts have called the worst in Mir's 11-year history.

One of the two Russian cosmonauts aboard said the crew thought it was possible to enter the punctured module wearing a spacesuit and that they could also reach the broken solar panel. Officials have said repairing the damage, which has sharply reduced Mir's power supply, may require a space walk.
